questions.stem:
Figure 2

A sprinter runs a race of 200 m. Her total time for running the race is 25 s. Figure 2 is a sketch of the speed-time graph for the motion of the sprinter. She starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to a speed of 9 m s$^{-1}$ in 4 s. The speed of 9 m s$^{-1}$ is maintained for 16 s and she then decelerates uniformly to a speed of $u$ m s$^{-1}$ at the end of the race. Calculate

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the distance covered by the sprinter in the first 20 s of the race,
(2)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Distance over last 5 s $= \frac{1}{2}(9+u) \times 5$ M1
$162 + \frac{1}{2}(9+u) \times 5 = 200$ M1 A1$\surd$
$\Rightarrow u = \underline{6.2\,\text{m s}^{-1}}$ A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the deceleration of the sprinter in the last 5 s of the race.
(3)

questions.question_text:
Figure 2

A sprinter runs a race of 200 m. Her total time for running the race is 25 s. Figure 2 is a sketch of the speed-time graph for the motion of the sprinter. She starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to a speed of 9 m s$^{-1}$ in 4 s. The speed of 9 m s$^{-1}$ is maintained for 16 s and she then decelerates uniformly to a speed of $u$ m s$^{-1}$ at the end of the race. Calculate
(a) the distance covered by the sprinter in the first 20 s of the race,
(2)
(b) the value of $u$,
(4)
(c) the deceleration of the sprinter in the last 5 s of the race.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) Distance $= \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 9 + 16 \times 9$ or $\frac{1}{2}(20+16) \times 9$ M1
$= \underline{162\,\text{m}}$ A1
(b) Distance over last 5 s $= \frac{1}{2}(9+u) \times 5$ M1
$162 + \frac{1}{2}(9+u) \times 5 = 200$ M1 A1$\surd$
$\Rightarrow u = \underline{6.2\,\text{m s}^{-1}}$ A1
(c) $6.2 = 9 + 5a$ M1 A1$\surd$
$a = (-)\underline{0.56\,\text{m s}^{-2}}$ A1

questions.stem:
Figure 3

A particle $P$ of mass 2.5 kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane under the action of a force of magnitude $X$ newtons acting up a line of greatest slope of the plane, as shown in Figure 3. The plane is inclined at $20°$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.4. The particle is in limiting equilibrium and is on the point of moving up the plane. Calculate

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the normal reaction of the plane on $P$,
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The force of magnitude $X$ newtons is now removed.
(c) Show that $P$ remains in equilibrium on the plane.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) In equilib. $F = 2.5g\sin 20 \approx 8.38 \text{ or } 8.4\,\text{N}$ B1
$\mu R = 0.4 \times 2.5g\cos 20 \approx 9.21 \text{ or } 9.2\,\text{N}$ B1
$8.4 < 9.2$ (using '$F < \mu R$' not $F = \mu R$) M1
Since $F < \mu R$ remains in equilibrium (cso) A1

A particle $P$ of mass 2.5 kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane under the action of a force of magnitude $X$ newtons acting up a line of greatest slope of the plane, as shown in Figure 3. The plane is inclined at $20°$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.4. The particle is in limiting equilibrium and is on the point of moving up the plane. Calculate
(a) the normal reaction of the plane on $P$,
(2)
(b) the value of $X$.
(4)
The force of magnitude $X$ newtons is now removed.
(c) Show that $P$ remains in equilibrium on the plane.
(4)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $R = 2.5g\cos 20$ M1
$\approx \underline{23.0 \text{ or } 23\,\text{N}}$ A1
(b) $X = 0.4 \times 23.0 + 2.5g\sin 20$ M1 A2,1,0$\surd$
$\approx \underline{17.6 \text{ or } 18\,\text{N}}$ A1
(c) In equilib. $F = 2.5g\sin 20 \approx 8.38 \text{ or } 8.4\,\text{N}$ B1
$\mu R = 0.4 \times 2.5g\cos 20 \approx 9.21 \text{ or } 9.2\,\text{N}$ B1
$8.4 < 9.2$ (using '$F < \mu R$' not $F = \mu R$) M1
Since $F < \mu R$ remains in equilibrium (cso) A1

The string passes over a small smooth pulley $P$ fixed at the edge of the table. The other end of the string is attached to a ball $B$ of mass 0.8 kg which hangs freely below the pulley, as shown in Figure 4. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the table is $\mu$. The system is released from rest with the string taut. After release, $B$ descends a distance of 0.4 m in 0.5 s. Modelling $A$ and $B$ as particles, calculate

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

N2L for $A$: $T - F = 0.5a$ M1 A1

The string passes over a small smooth pulley $P$ fixed at the edge of the table. The other end of the string is attached to a ball $B$ of mass 0.8 kg which hangs freely below the pulley, as shown in Figure 4. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and the table is $\mu$. The system is released from rest with the string taut. After release, $B$ descends a distance of 0.4 m in 0.5 s. Modelling $A$ and $B$ as particles, calculate
(a) the acceleration of $B$,
(3)
(b) the tension in the string,

questions.question_text:
Two ships $P$ and $Q$ are travelling at night with constant velocities. At midnight, $P$ is at the point with position vector $(20\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j})$ km relative to a fixed origin $O$. At the same time, $Q$ is at the point with position vector $(14\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j})$ km. Three hours later, $P$ is at the point with position vector $(29\mathbf{i}+34\mathbf{j})$ km. The ship $Q$ travels with velocity $12\mathbf{j}$ km h$^{-1}$. At time $t$ hours after midnight, the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$ are $\mathbf{p}$ km and $\mathbf{q}$ km respectively. Find
(a) the velocity of $P$, in terms of $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$,
(2)
(b) expressions for $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$, in terms of $t$, $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.
(4)
At time $t$ hours after midnight, the distance between $P$ and $Q$ is $d$ km.
(c) By finding an expression for $\overrightarrow{PQ}$, show that
$$d^2 = 25t^2-92t+292.$$
(5)
Weather conditions are such that an observer on $P$ can only see the lights on $Q$ when the distance between $P$ and $Q$ is 15 km or less. Given that when $t=1$, the lights on $Q$ move into sight of the observer,
(d) find the time, to the nearest minute, at which the lights on $Q$ move out of sight of the observer.
(5)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\mathbf{v}_P = \{(29\mathbf{i}+34\mathbf{j})-(20\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j})\}/3 = \underline{(3\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})\,\text{km h}^{-1}}$ M1 A1
(b) $\mathbf{p} = (20\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j}) + (3\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})t$ M1 A1$\surd$
$\mathbf{q} = (14\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}) + 12t\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
(c) $\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p} = (-6-3t)\mathbf{i} + (-16+4t)\mathbf{j}$ M1 A1
$d^2 = (-6-3t)^2 + (-16+4t)^2$ M1
$= 36+36t+9t^2+16t^2-128t+256$ M1
$= 25t^2-92t+292$ (*) A1 (cso)
(d) $25t^2-92t+292 = 225$ M1
$25t^2-92t+67 = 0$ A1
$(t-1)(25t-67) = 0$ M1
$t = 67/25 \text{ or } 2.68$ A1
time $\approx$ 161 mins, or 2 hrs 41 mins, or 2.41 am, or 0241 A1
